stories_kpis.Explanation: Remaining performance obligations representing expected future revenues from executed contracts
stories_kpis.Signal: Strong order growth driven by CEC acquisition and E-Infrastructure Solutions demand
stories_kpis.Description: Le carnet de commandes de 3,01 milliards de dollars reflète une croissance exceptionnelle de 78% stimulée par l'acquisition stratégique de CEC (488,9 millions) et la demande continue dans les data centers et les solutions d'infrastructure électrique.

ai_positioning.summary: Sterling Infrastructure recognizes artificial intelligence as a growth driver for its E-Infrastructure Solutions segment through increasing adoption in cloud computing and digital transformation projects for hyperscaler data centers.
evidence: Investments driven by 'increasing adoption and complexity of artificial intelligence applications and digital transformation across industries'
Data center customer capital deployment plans supporting cloud computing and AI implementation
ai_positioning.source: 10-K MD&A - Market Outlook and Trends, E-Infrastructure Solutions section

risks.title: Interest Rate Risk
risks.score_rationale: At December 31, 2025, variable rate debt of $292.5 million means a 100-basis point increase in interest rates would increase annual interest expense by approximately $2.9 million. This is a manageable risk given the company's strong cash position of $390.7 million and improving profitability.
risks.summary: Variable rate debt exposure of $292.5 million creates interest rate sensitivity, but strong cash generation mitigates this risk.

risks.title: Long-Lived Asset Impairment
risks.score_rationale: The company's acquisitions of Drake ($25M) and CEC ($562M) introduce goodwill and intangible assets that could be subject to impairment if acquired businesses underperform. Management assessed no impairment in 2025, 2024, or 2023, but integration risks exist.
risks.summary: Significant recent acquisitions create potential for asset impairment if operational targets are not achieved, though no indicators present as of year-end 2025.

risks.title: Residential Building Demand Cyclicality
risks.score_rationale: Building Solutions segment faced declining demand starting in Q2 2024 due to homebuyer affordability challenges. Management expects near-term muted demand, though long-term demographics support recovery. This segment represents meaningful revenue contribution.
risks.summary: Residential market headwinds from affordability challenges create near-term revenue pressure on Building Solutions segment despite favorable long-term demographics.

risks.title: RHB Deconsolidation Revenue Loss
risks.score_rationale: RHB deconsolidation effective January 1, 2025 removed $235.9 million of 2024 revenue from 2025 comparables. However, organic revenue growth of 17.7% (excluding this impact) demonstrates underlying business strength. Future RHB earnings will be recognized as equity method income.
risks.summary: Accounting change for RHB joint venture (from consolidation to equity method) removes approximately $236M in annual revenue visibility but reflects ownership structure clarification.

risks.title: Backlog Conversion and Margin Realization
risks.score_rationale: Despite strong backlog growth to $3.01B (+78%), the company must successfully execute projects to convert this into earnings. Backlog margin of 17.8% provides visibility, but execution risks in large E-Infrastructure projects exist, particularly in newly acquired CEC operations.
risks.summary: Converting $3.01 billion backlog into profit requires successful project execution and margin realization, particularly for large-scale E-Infrastructure Solutions projects.
